claim_text: Spotify had a login outage on the morning of Tuesday, Nov 24, that logged many users out and stopped them signing back in
summary: From about 6:15 AM ET on Nov 24, many Spotify users in several countries were logged out and could not sign back in. TechRadar's reporter was logged out of the iOS app and could not log back in.
detail: TechRadar saw the problem first-hand. Numerama, Digit and RIA Novosti each read Downdetector's report counts and describe mostly login failures, with some app and playback problems. Some users were asked to set up a new account instead of signing in. Numerama says offline downloads could still play if the session had not been closed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A first-hand check by one outlet and separate report-tracker readings by three more outlets agree on the outage.

claim_text: Downdetector showed more than 16,500 reports in the US and more than 8,000 in the UK at the peak
summary: TechRadar reported over 16,500 Downdetector reports in the US and over 8,000 in the UK at about 6:58 AM ET. Digit gives a US peak of 16,451 against a baseline of eight.
detail: These are user-submitted reports, not a count of affected users. We did not read Downdetector ourselves. Digit's peak times are in India time. Reuters, carried by Khaleej Times, gives a peak of more than 14,000 at about 6:45 AM ET; the outlets read the tracker at different times.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets relay Downdetector's counts; the peaks are close but not the same.

claim_text: Users in at least a dozen countries reported problems, mostly with logging in
summary: RIA Novosti lists Downdetector reports from the US (10,600), Germany (6,100), the UK (4,600), the Netherlands (2,700), Italy (1,900) and other countries. Numerama counts 2,000+ in France; Digit about 800 in India.
detail: Counts were taken at different times by each outlet, so they do not add up. Digit says about 70% of US reports were about logging in; Sunday Guardian gives 68%; Numerama, citing the tracker Instatus, gives 61% at the peak.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets read user-report trackers in different countries.

claim_text: Spotify's status account said it was aware of issues and was checking them out
summary: Spotify's official status account on X posted: "We're aware of some issues right now and are checking them out!" The post is timestamped 6:56 AM ET. TechRadar and Numerama both show it.
detail: It gives no cause. Numerama says Spotify's status page showed no incident; we did not use that page.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Spotify's own post, and two independent outlets that each show it.
notes: The post is on a social platform; the outlets are cited for it.

claim_text: Sign-ins were working again for most users by about 7:15 AM ET
summary: Spotify posted "Everything's looking much better now" at 7:08 AM ET and said at 10:53 AM ET that the issue was resolved. TechRadar could sign in by about 7:15 AM ET; Reuters had reports down to about 600 by 7:17 AM ET.
detail: The outage lasted roughly an hour. Spotify's 10:53 AM ET post says the issue was resolved but gives no exact end time. Android Authority and TechPulse said some users still reported trouble signing in after Spotify's 7:08 AM post. Tom's Guide also said the problems were over. USA Today reported Downdetector reports had fallen to a few hundred by 7:30 AM ET. The Verge said at about noon ET that some people were still logged out and getting a "something went wrong, try again" message, and that Spotify was pointing them to a support-forum thread.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: TechRadar's first-hand check, Reuters, Tom's Guide and USA Today independently report the recovery, and Spotify's own posts say things are much better and, later, that the issue was resolved.

claim_text: The cause of the Nov 24 login outage
summary: Spotify has not said what caused the outage. No source we read gives a cause.
detail: TechRadar, Numerama, Digit, Android Authority and TechPulse each say Spotify had not explained the problem. Numerama's update says the company gave no explanation of where the outage came from.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Five outlets report that Spotify gave no cause.

claim_text: No source we read says the Spotify outage was a cyberattack, or rules one out
summary: We found no claim of responsibility, no DDoS claim, no report of an attack and no Spotify statement on the cause. We also found no statement ruling an attack out. Being logged out is not by itself a sign of a hack.
detail: A search for a hack or DDoS claim about Spotify on Nov 24 found none. None of the outlets we read reports an attack, and Spotify's three status posts do not mention one.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources gives a cause or reports an attack.

claim_text: The start time differs between sources, from about 5:30 to 6:34 AM ET
summary: TechRadar says problems started at about 6:15 AM ET. Android Authority and Tom's Guide say about 5:30 AM ET. Numerama says US problems began at 6:34 AM ET, and RIA Novosti says complaints began about 2:32 PM Moscow time (6:32 AM ET).
detail: The outlets read report trackers at different times. Tom's Guide pairs 5:30 AM ET with 11:30 GMT, which is 6:30 AM ET, so its time may be off by an hour; TechPulse gives 11:30 Belgian time (5:30 AM ET). The difference does not change the finding.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets give different start times.

claim_text: Outlets said the wrong-password errors did not by themselves mean users' accounts had been hacked
summary: Some users were told their password was wrong and feared a hack. Android Authority said affected users' accounts had likely not been hacked, and TechPulse said there was no sign so far that accounts were hacked.
detail: Both outlets advised waiting rather than resetting passwords. This is their reading of the errors, not a Spotify statement, and it does not say what caused the outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets give the same reading of the errors; neither cites Spotify for it.

claim_text: Spotify told users who had been logged out to sign back in with their original login details
summary: In its 10:53 AM ET post, Spotify's status account said users who were logged out should log back in "using your original login credentials". Radiónica and The Verge relay the same post.
detail: The post gives no cause and does not say whether any accounts were affected or whether Spotify found any sign of an attack. Users still having trouble were pointed to Spotify's community support thread and customer support.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Spotify's own post on X, relayed by two outlets. Outlets relaying one statement count as one source, and a social post counts as Tier 4, so this stays Reported.
